parameters.content:
## Waitlist 01 - Response Page

Serves the page somebody lands on from the waitlist offer email. **GET only, and it writes nothing.**

Corporate mail scanners fetch every link before the recipient sees it. If this endpoint recorded anything, the first scanner to walk the link would answer on the recipient's behalf. Recording happens in **Waitlist 02 - Response Handler**, on POST.

### Seven outcomes, three shapes of page

**The form**, when the offer is open: the event, when and where, how long the place is held, and two submit buttons.

**A close-off page**, when there is simply nothing left to do: already accepted, already declined, expired, or event now full.

**A refusal page**, when something is genuinely wrong, which ends by pointing at a human: no row matches the token, or the row's status is not one this page can act on.

Expiry is judged two ways, either the row saying `expired` or its `expires_at` having passed, because the row is not corrected until the hourly sweep catches it. Capacity is read at the moment of the click, and Waitlist 02 reads it again at submit time, because somebody else can accept in between.

### Why buttons rather than links

A scanner can fetch a page. It cannot press a submit button. That is why recording lives behind a POST, and why the offer email carries one link to this page rather than two links that act.

### Two known limitations

**`IF Fetch Errors?` catches GraphQL errors, not transport failures.** `Fetch Event` runs `continueRegularOutput`, so a timeout produces an item with no `errors` array and the page still renders, just without the date and location. A form the reader can act on beats an error page.

**`Log Failure` passes an empty `nodeId` when no row was found**, so on that path the log call fails silently. Waitlist 03 handles the same case explicitly.

### Setup

1. Attach the Administrate OAuth2 credential to **Fetch Event** and **Log Failure**.
2. Confirm SUBMIT_URL matches the production webhook URL of Waitlist 02.
3. Publish so the webhook is live, and copy this workflow's production webhook URL into RESPONSE_PAGE_URL in Waitlist Automation.

### Testing

Open a real offer link in a **browser**. `ignoreBots` is on, which returns 403 to anything without a browser User-Agent, so curl or an HTTP client will look broken when it is not.

Check that the event title, date and location all resolve. A blank title means the row carries an event id the instance no longer has.

### Why there is no success log

This workflow performs no mutation, so there is no outcome to record. Failures on the read are logged. Page views are not, because a scanner opening a link is not worth writing to the event record.

## Config Explained

**GRAPHQL_URL** - the Administrate API endpoint. The same for every instance.

**ORIGIN_IDENTIFIER** - the name entries appear under in the Administrate event log. **Should be identical across all five waitlist workflows** so the history reads as one story. Use the status field, not the origin, to tell entries apart.

**OFFERS_TABLE_ID** - the id of your `waitlist_offers` Data Table. **Load Row** reads this value through an expression, so changing it here is the whole change. Do **not** re-select the table in the node: that replaces the expression with a hardcoded id.

**SUBMIT_URL** - where the form posts: the production webhook URL of **Waitlist 02 - Response Handler**. If that path changes, update this, or every submission goes nowhere.

**ACCEPT_ACTION** and **DECLINE_ACTION** - the values the two buttons post. They must match the same two values in Waitlist 02's Config exactly, or a valid answer comes back as unrecognized.

**ACCEPT_LABEL** and **DECLINE_LABEL** - the wording on the buttons.

**BRAND_NAME** - the wordmark at the top of every page. Set it to your organisation's name.

**BRAND_CSS** - all styling for the pages this workflow serves. Change colours and spacing here, not in Render Page. This is a page stylesheet and **cannot** be reused in the offer email, which needs table layout and inline styles because mail clients strip a style block.

### The palette

The CSS variables at the top drive everything: `--b` masthead and primary button, `--a` keyline under the masthead and focus ring, `--t` notice panel, plus a red pair for the error variant. Keep text on `--b` legible (white text needs a dark background); a bright accent colour should accent rather than fill.
